item.description:
Costco has officially revealed its annual Holiday Savings ad and you can already start browsing what will be discounted this year. Similar to other retailers, Costco is offering multiple waves of savings leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday. The first wave of sales kicked off on October 30 and will run through November 15.
Costco Black Friday Sale Schedule
According to Costco's official page, most the deals will be available both in-warehouse or online except for on Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday. You can check out the full schedule below and click on each link to check out the ads for each sale.
Pre-pre-Thanksgiving Day Sale - October 30 - November 15
Pre-Thanksgiving Day Sale - October 16 - November 30
Thanksgivng Day Sale - November 26 (Online Only)
Black Friday Sale - November 27-30
Cyber Monday Sale - November 30 (Online Only)
What are some of the best deals?
The different sales have a pretty varied selection of deals, so there are savings to be had pretty much all month long. The pre-pre-Thanksgiving sale that's happening now and the pre-thanksgiving sale both have a good amount of deals on snacks, frozen foods, and kitchen essentials. There's also a decent number of discounts on TVs and gaming monitors during this time, all of which will last until Cyber Monday if they stay in stock.
As you might expect, some of the best deals on tech and other big-ticket items don't arrive until the actual Black Friday sale kicks off after Thanksgiving. This is when you'll find an RTX 5060 gaming PC for $300 off, a Dyson vacuum under $300, and a great 4K TV for under $1,000. This is also when some of the best frozen food deals happen, including $5 off Costco's signature frozen lasagnas.
Both the individual Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday sales offer a few interesting items, but the bulk of the sale is not there. If you need a pair of Dickies men's overalls or cargo pants for $30, you won't want to miss the Thanksgiving sale. And if you plan on eating at Applebee's a lot in the future, the Cyber Monday gift card deal is definitely worth taking a look at.
More Black Friday Sales Announced
Costco isn't the only one currently running a holiday sale before Halloween. Best Buy just kicked off its DoorBOOster sale after announcing the full Best By Black Friday schedule for 2026. Both Walmart and Target have also announced their sale dates for November. It's already looking like a busy month for anyone looking to save as much as possible this year.

item.title: By Skipping Last-Gen Systems, Stranger Than Heaven is Allowing RGG Studio to Fully Leverage the Power of Current-Gen Consoles at Long Last
item.description:
Stranger Than Heaven will apparently be the most technically accomplished game that developer RGG Studio has ever produced, and that’s largely due to the fact that it's being created solely for current generation hardware. The game’s producer, Hiroyuki Sakamoto, confirmed as much to IGN during an interview conducted at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 this week.
“We set out to make Stranger Than Heaven as a completely brand-new game, with the goal of creating something entirely fresh while putting forth the absolute best quality we can produce right now,” explained Sakamoto. “[So] we decided to drop previous-gen platforms like the PS4 and focus on creating an experience best enjoyed natively on current-gen consoles like the PS5.”
Since the launch of the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S systems back in 2020, all of RGG Studio’s games have still kept one foot stuck in the previous console generation. 2024’s Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth was developed to run across two eras of PlayStation and Xbox, and while Xbox One was finally dropped for Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties earlier this year, support for PlayStation 4 remained.
However, by developing Stranger Than Heaven purely for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, the team hasn’t had to make any hardware-based compromises to its vision for the new game’s multiple decade-spanning journey through early 20th century Japan.
“In the past, hardware constraints meant limiting the number of characters we could display on screen at once, among other things we had to give up on,” continued Sakamoto. “With Stranger Than Heaven, by fully leveraging the PS5's capabilities we were able to showcase more characters on screen simultaneously than ever before and raise character quality to the next level.”
Despite some lingering reservations regarding its digital resurrection of the late rapper Tupac Shakur, IGN's Michael Higham found a lot to like about Stranger Than Heaven in his recent hands-on preview. With just over two months to go before its scheduled release in January, Sakamato seems supremely confident in where the game is at, going on to state, “I think we succeeded in achieving our goal of creating a richer visual experience with a stronger artistic identity than anything we've done prior.”
During the same chat, Sakamoto also confirmed the inclusion of in-game “cheats” in Stranger Than Heaven that you can read about here.
Stranger Than Heaven is set for release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC on January 15, 2027.

item.title: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
item.description:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.
In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.
Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with several bonus items, which will be revealed later in the Fan Fest keynote - I will update this as they are shown. Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.
There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series, a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.

item.title: Stranger Than Heaven Features Optional “Cheats” to Make its Combat Easier
item.description:
Stranger Than Heaven, the upcoming street-brawler from the makers of Yakuza and Like a Dragon, will feature optional in-game assists to make its challenging new combat system more approachable, developer RGG Studio has confirmed to IGN in an interview conducted at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 this week.
In IGN’s most recent hands-on with the game, my colleague Michael Higham described Stranger Than Heaven’s parry-based combat system as “demanding”, adding that “you really have to pay attention to attack animations not just for timing, but to make the correct call on the direction it's coming from.” This initially seemed like it could prove to be divisive among fans of the comparatively carefree button-mashing combo systems found in RRG Studios’ previous adventures like Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii and Lost Judgment, but it turns out that Stranger Than Heaven’s more complex combat system will only be as difficult as players want it to be.
Stranger Than Heaven Screenshots
“We knew mechanics like parrying would be challenging, but based on feedback from players who tried the hands-on demos at various game shows, like [Gamescom Asia], we’ve fine-tuned details like difficulty balance and control responsiveness,” said Hiroyuki Sakamoto, producer of Stranger Than Heaven. "We've also included difficulty settings and provided plenty of support features, such as cheat items that increase health regeneration. We believe that if we offer enough support for action-game beginners, it will give them the chance to play through to the very end.”
Sakamoto insisted that with some perseverance from players and the inclusion of a lengthy tutorial phase in the early stages of the game to help them, he hoped that most players will eventually start to enjoy the new mechanics. He also stated that the highest difficulty setting is "extremely challenging," so the more battle-hardened gamers will still be able to face a more unforgiving combat experience should they so choose. However, for players who perhaps want to purely focus on enjoying the multiple decade-spanning story and the showbiz-based side activities without mastering the rhythm of the combat, the addition of the cheat items should mean that all fans of RGG Studio’s games will be able to enjoy Stranger Than Heaven.
“Equipping those cheat items makes you much harder to defeat by automatically restoring health and providing other perks,” explained Sakamoto. “For beginners who still struggle with blocking, we’re prepared assistance items that let you clear encounters using basic left and right punches alone.”
There is one small catch to using these assist items, however, but it’s a fairly humorous one in typically cheeky RGG Studio style.
“You can obtain [the cheat items] right from the start of the game,” said Sakamoto. “But because they function as ‘handicap’ items and you wear it as a cloth/garment, anyone watching your gameplay screen will immediately notice you’re wearing them.”
So no activating cheats and pretending to be an absolute parry-beast on a livestream, then.
Stranger Than Heaven is set for release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC on January 15, 2027.

item.title: Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games posted a chilling warning on its social media pages, warning that the studio might close before it can launch the Early Access version of its medieval open-world action/strategy sandbox because funding for the team is "no longer in place."
item.description:
Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games posted a chilling warning on its social media pages, warning that the studio might close before it can launch the Early Access version of its medieval open-world action/strategy sandbox because funding for the team is "no longer in place."
In a message on X (with a hat tip to Insider Gaming), Raw Power laid out its unfortunate predicament: "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding behind Raw Power Games is no longer in place. Without it we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing. We're not going to sugarcoat. You deserve to hear it plainly, and directly from us.
"What makes it hurt is how close we are," the message continued. "Early Access is within reach. The world we've been building for years is finally starting to feel alive, and we have so much we've been thrilled to show you. Every day in the studio – in Copenhagen and remote – we've seen people put everything they have into this game, often far beyond what anyone asked of them. They are the ones carrying the heaviest weight right now, and we couldn't be prouder of them. We don't know yet how this ends. But in the spirit of our game we're not going down without a fight!"
Chronicles: Medieval's Tom Hardy-narrated announcement trailer drew a lot of interest, netting more than 2 million views on IGN's YouTube channel. It was revealed at Summer Game Fest 2025, and we have since previewed it not once but twice. In our most recent hands-on, we noted that it still felt pretty early at the time, but also said, "The scale and detail of the battles simultaneously is very impressive," and, "Being able to jump into a commander at ground level for more of a third-person action mode is really cool."
Raw Power Games told fans, "If you want to stand with us, keep Chronicles: Medieval on your wishlist and keep talking about it. It matters more right now than you might think. Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for believing in this game. We really hope you'll get to play the world we've been creating."
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.
item.description:
Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.
At a press event earlier this week for id Software's Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which was released this summer, studio co-director Marty Stratton was asked how the studio is doing in the wake of the layoffs that affected id as part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's ongoing Xbox "reset." He answered, "We're doing great. Not to handwave the [layoffs] away...everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department.
"We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever. We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead."
This is purely speculative on my part, but might the two decorated first-person shooter studios be co-developing MachineGames's next project, which is heavily rumored to be Wolfenstein 3 – with studio head Jerk Gustafsson saying, "We're not done with Wolfenstein yet"? Not only has MachineGames used id Software's idTech engine for every one of its games, but Sharma has publicly stated that she wants Xbox's development teams to double down on their biggest franchises – a sentiment echoed by Bethesda boss Jill Braff. And with id now seemingly done with Doom: The Dark Ages following the oustanding Revelations DLC, a team-up with MachineGames might help get the rumored third Wolfenstein game out the door faster, and getting games out more quickly is one of Sharma's goals.
In addition, while Doom should certainly be considered in that "biggest franchises" group, Wolfenstein most likely is as well. Plus, Amazon has a Wolfenstein TV series in development, which might further incentivize Xbox and Bethesda to pair up id and MachineGames to make sure the latter team's next game is as awesome – and out as quickly – as possible. Bu whatever either team does next, the project(s) will be highly anticipated, at least by me, as both teams have incredible track records, both historically and recently.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance.
item.description:
Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima showed up for a cameo role in a new animated short from legendary rock outfit My Chemical Romance.
That's probably not the first sentence you expected to read heading into the Halloween weekend, but considering Kojima is known for his love of music, movies, games, and everything in between, it may not be too surprising. Still, fans of his work as a creative powerhouse were probably shocked to see him appear in the credits for the band's new animated short film, Prelude to The End.
The seven-and-a-half-minute project, which arrived as a surprise drop yesterday evening, is a stop-motion, dark fairytale based on director Lauren Tsai's The Dying World. Serving as a vehicle for a 20th anniversary music video for My Chemical Romance's "The End." – the opening track for the New Jersey group's seminal rock record, The Black Parade – the video also enlisted Kojima for a quick voice role.
Just as main character, Astrid, retreats to her room to parse through a few missed calls, we get Kojima's My Chemical Romance music video debut. He's credited simply as The Teacher, and can be heard scolding Astrid about late work in her third voicemail. You can see the full text below.
"Astrid your Japanese homework is late again. This is unacceptab-" Kojima's The Teacher can be heard saying before the recording is cut off.
Kojima is far from a stranger when it comes to cameos, but he's been especially busy in this department lately. The Metal Gear Solid series, which Kojima created and orchestrated for years, features a few moments where he broke the fourth wall for a cameo. He also appeared in CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 for a role that he recently reprised in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.
https://t.co/MjeYkDAgV5
Kojima's collaboration with My Chemical Romance might have been especially exciting for the game creator, though, as his love for the band's music is well-documented. After posting about some of his favorite merch in early 2022, he shared that he attended one of the band's concerts in 2022. At the time, he said, "When I went to the venue, there were almost all teenage girls. I didn't see any old men in my age. But as I was wearing the band T-shirt, people said to me 'I like your T-shirt, Ojisan.'
Kojima also secretly teased his involvement in Prelude to The End when mentioning he had picked up the 20th Anniversary Edition of The Black Parade on vinyl just a few days ago. He then celebrated his involvement in the video with another post on X/Twitter.
Kojima is in good company when it comes to his My Chemical Romance cameo. Also featured in the list of Astrid's missed voicemails are Lost Weekend songwriter Phoebe Bridgers and Hit Me Hard and Soft hitmaker Billie Eilish. With both Grammy-Award-winning artists sharing a few seconds with Kojima, the moment definitely made sure to pack in as many heavy hitters as it could.
Kojima will seemingly continue to show up in side projects as he stays focused on other projects, including OD and Physint. Last night, we also got the first trailer for the anime spinoff series, Death Stranding Isolations. We know the Kojima Productions mastermind will appear in one live-action cameo, too, though what it will be has yet to be revealed.

item.title: As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
item.description:
As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post, outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture.
"We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight."
Marathon Screenshots 2026 and 2025
It's the "nothing can help us bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable" bit that's got the Destiny community so riled up. With the back-and-forth pulling Destiny 2 in and out of the fire all through the span of a few months, some believed Bungie was trying to tell its audience that picking up a copy of its new sci-fi FPS would help keep it and the studio's future secure. Deane stepped in to confirm this is not the case.
The Bungie developer said his intention was not to rest the Destiny revival on the shoulders of the fans that helped breathe life back into it earlier this year. He chalks it up to a mistranslation, "and that's on me."
"In no way is the Destiny plan contingent upon Marathon," Deane added. "Play what inspires you, whatever it is. Mainly hoping we can accomplish our goals in both lanes with a stronger relationship with our entire community!"
I may have worded this clumsily but this is the true heart of what I was trying to say Truly care about community healing and believe that it will help our studio bridge into the future in the most healthy way possible ❤️Play and share what you are passionate about, whatever that isThe Destiny plan moves forward no matter what
When one player suggested they feared they were being encouraged to purchase but never download Marathon just to support Bungie, Deane said, "Oh, don't buy Marathon as a donation or offer anything else."
"It's our job to show up for you," he added. When another fan expressed similar concern, he said, "I truly love the sentiment but only buy or play a thing that inspires you from us / you think is cool! We will find our way back home with Destiny."
So, there you have it: Destiny and Marathon don't depend upon the success of the other. As Bungie principal comms manager Dylan Gafner said, "Two cakes! One big community." That should offer some relief not only to Destiny players who feared their favorite game's future may still be in jeopardy but also to Marathon players who have feared the same.
Negativity has surrounded both games in recent months, with community members on each side going at each other as both struggled. For now, we know that the Destiny franchise will live on with a few projects. These include "celebration" content updates, a project that the team has teased as "Destiny 'Legacy'," and a mysterious "redacted" project.
For Marathon, Bungie will continue to try to revitalize the extraction shooter with Symbiosis this December. The studio also recently reassured players that the extraction component is "still a major part" of the experience as the team experiments with PvE and Deathmatch modes.
What's next for Destiny and Marathon remains to be seen, but it's clear Bungie is putting in the work to keep both afloat. While we wait to see how things pan out, you can see why the studio believes the latter struggled at launch. You can also read about how the Destiny community banded together to help the #SaveMassEffect movement.

item.title: The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.
item.description:
The developers of VRChat have created a rift in the virtual platform’s user base after announcing that it would not include labels to categorize AI-generated content, despite around 95% of users asking for some sort of AI filter in a survey.
VRChat is a virtual hub where folks can gather to chat, make their own avatars, and create and play games together. It’s a fairly popular social platform that, perhaps unsurprisingly, is a hotbed for viral moments and hilarious content.
Also unsurprisingly, there’s been a sharp increase in AI-generated content in VRChat, to the point where fans are begging for some sort of distinction as to what has and hasn’t been made by humans.
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Dual Destinies VR Screenshots
In fact, the folks behind VRChat recently published a survey asking users for their feedback on the state of the platform. In that survey, “95% of survey respondents want some kind of label for AI usage,” as told in an official blog published on October 28.
Despite this overwhelming majority, the powers that be have decided against moving forward with an AI label, arguing that there’s simply too much disagreement among users as to what, exactly, should be done to delineate such content.
“We’re not adding an ‘AI-generated’ label or AI filters,” the devs said in the blog post. “While we think some creators would honestly label their content, we think others would try to pass off generative or assisted work as completely authored by hand. Likewise, we could see this creating ‘sleuthing’ behavior, where folks would attempt to sniff out ‘AI’ content or might harass other creators, even if they are genuinely not using any AI tools in their workflow. We think this potentially creates negative behavior spirals we don’t want to encourage.”
The statement continued, revealing that respondents gave “3,141 different combinations of labeling,”and that “no single combination was given by more than 10% of respondents.”
Essentially, the team at VRChat feels they need to “understand this a layer deeper before making any kneejerk decisions” — but their explanation hasn’t been well-received by fans.
On social media, dedicated VRChat users are speaking out against this decision, with one writing on X/Twitter, “Then what was the point of the survey if they’re not going to f**king use it to influence decisions?”
How interested are you in VR gaming today?

item.title: The Band of the Grenadier Guards performed a medley of Star Trek themes in honor of Sir Patrick Stewart – none of which were the theme music of the show the late actor starred in.
item.description:
Tributes to the late Sir Patrick Stewart quickly poured in after his death was announced Thursday, with his colleagues from the Star Trek and Marvel franchises sharing their condolences and memories of the actor who played Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard.
In a move worthy of the famous meme of Captain Picard holding his brow, Buckingham Palace in London paid a moving tribute to Stewart on Friday, but in an unintentionally mistaken way.
The Band of the Grenadier Guards performed a medley of Star Trek themes in honor of the actor – none of which were the theme music of the show he starred in.
Buckingham Palace Honours Sir Patrick Stewart (1940–2026) with Star Trek Theme Tune 🕊️The Band of the Grenadier Guards performs the iconic Star Trek theme at Buckingham Palace in honour of Sir Patrick Stewart, following the sad news of his passing.Queen Elizabeth II knighted Sir Patrick Stewart in 2010, recognising his outstanding contribution to drama and the arts 🇬🇧🎥 @KingsGuardTours📆 30 October 2026📍 Buckingham Palace#SirPatrickStewart #StarTrek #GrenadierGuards #BuckinghamPalace #BritishArmyMusic
Instead of playing the theme music of Star Trek: The Next Generation, the guards instead played the theme music from the William Shatner-led original Star Trek series before segueing to the theme from the J.J. Abrams-produced movie reboot trilogy.
Well, it’s the thought that counts. As Captain Picard would say, “We're only mortal.”
While Star Trek and X-Men may have made him a household name, please read why Patrick Stewart’s best roles in film and television went beyond outer space and mutants.
Stewart also left his mark on video games. Bethesda and Oblivion fans also paid tribute to Stewart in the wake of his death, while Star Trek Online players honored the Picard star in-game.
In Pictures: Sir Patrick Stewart
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog.
item.description:
An animal rescuer is condemning vandals who spray-painted a hedgehog blue, presumably to make it look like Sega’s beloved mascot character, Sonic the Hedgehog.
The heartbreaking story comes from West Yorkshire in the UK, where a male hedgehog was found with extensive chemical burns after being spray-painted blue by supposed vandals. The animal was discovered outside the Wakefield police station and subsequently brought to Castleford Hedgehog Rescue on Tuesday, October 27, for treatment.
Unfortunately, the poor critter didn’t make it. Local reports state that the spray paint literally burned through “several layers” of the hedgehog’s skin, to the point where it melted its spines, causing extreme pain.
29-year-old Beth Campbell, who operates the hedgehog rescue, says she tried everything in her power to help — but the pain was so severe that the defenseless animal literally “screamed himself to death.”
"I don't know how anyone could be so cruel to an animal. It is disgusting,” she told YorkshireLive. "I haven't seen anything as bad or as sad as this in a long time. …I'm glad he was brought in, as it meant at least we could ease his suffering and make him feel comfortable."
Campbell says the spray paint gave the hedgehog significant chemical burns that, in turn, triggered an infection on its now-exposed skin. This, along with potential poisoning from the chemicals in the spray paint, is what ultimately caused its death.
Sonic the Hedgehog #91 Preview Gallery
She also revealed that the hedgehog was suffering from a condition known as flystrike, which occurs when flies lay their eggs in animals’ open wounds or soft tissue, resulting in maggots that feast on their flesh. Spray paint aside, Campbell said that the critter would have likely undergone a "slow and ultimately and extremely painful death" in the wild.
On Facebook, the hedgehog rescued posted a heartwrenching tribute to the deceased hedgehog: “As a result of cruelty our poor boy has passed away. This has deeply affected our volunteers and myself as he laid screaming in pain, he was given the full amount of pain relief he could have," the group wrote.
“Rest peacefully little man, the way you were treated was horrific, we tried everything we possibly could to save you, but you were too precious for this cruel world. Pain free, running free across the rainbow bridge.”
Campbell said she plans to report the incident to police, but is unsure if any action will be taken, given the location where the animal was found. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and local police have not released a statement regarding the matter.
Hedgehogs are listed as a nearly threatened species globally and are classified as vulnerable for extinction within the UK. Populations of the animal have dropped between 30-75% since 2000, with expanding human activity impacting their ability to find food, shelter, and otherwise survive.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resynced anytime soon.
item.description:
Ubisoft said more Assassin's Creed games are on the way, but don't expect to see remakes like Black Flag Resynced anytime soon.
The publisher behind the history-hopping stealth-action franchise laid all its cards on the table in a lengthy update post yesterday. Considering that this year's Assassin's Creed 4 remake seemed to go off without a hitch when it launched in July, one might assume re-imaginings for other games are on the way – but that is not the case.
When spelling out where Assassin's Creed has been and where it's heading, Ubisoft plainly addressed desires for more re-imaginings in a section called 'What About Other Remakes?' It knows Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has fans chomping at the bit for more, but it doesn't sound like we'll be getting any more for a very long time.
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Observe Gameplay and Blood Effects
"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," it said. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."
Why not revisit older games? Black Flag has remained a beloved installment in the franchise even more than a decade after its original release, but fans have continued to clamor to revisit stories from games like the original Assassin's Creed, Assassin's Creed 2, and Assassin's Creed 3. As happy with Black Flag Resynced as Ubisoft is, the publisher admitted that returning to the West Indies took more than a little legwork.
"As our first-ever franchise remake, Resynced taught us a tremendous amount," it explained. "Taking on a game that holds such a special place in players' hearts brought both excitement and challenges. Rebuilding old systems from scratch, adding new elements that fit the experience, and balancing legacy with innovation was a massive undertaking. We're super proud of what the Resynced team delivered and how well it was received."
The Complete Assassin's Creed Timeline
Unfortunately, we won't be donning Altair or Ezio's Assassin cloaks anytime soon. Still, just because no remakes are in development now, it doesn't mean there won't ever be an opportunity to return to fan-favorite worlds and stories.
"But don't mistake that for a closed door. Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back. That door remains open because, after all... Nothing is true, everything is permitted."
Of course, that doesn't mean the Creed is going anywhere. Ubisoft also acknowledged that its teams are "focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles," which includes projects fans "haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories." One of those is Codename Hexe, another game that it made sure to touch on in its update post. In May, the publisher said the plan was to deliver new games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Ghost Recon franchises over the course of the next few years.

item.title: Over the years, Reddit has become almost the default message board for most of the internet, and as such houses answers to thousands of questions that anyone could access, even without an account. However, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman has suggested that most of Reddit will end up locked behind a login screen.
item.description:
Over the years, Reddit has become almost the default message board for most of the internet and, as such, houses answers to thousands of questions that anyone could access, even without an account. However, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman has suggested that most of Reddit will end up locked behind a login screen.
In a post titled "About that login screen," Huffman talks about his decision to turn Reddit into a "primarily logged-in experience." In true Reddit fashion, he includes a TL;DR, where he says, "We’re making the change because it’s better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data. And we can do this while continuing to ensure user privacy." But I suspect that this all leads back to Google's AI overviews.
The first section of Huffman's long post is all about personalization, and it sounds like Reddit is going to use your account to build a personal algorithm, which will show you more of the content that you're interested in. That is extremely normal for any website in 2026. According to the post, "Our goal is to help you find what’s most relevant to you and drive the community, connection and belonging that makes Reddit, Reddit."
In the next section, Huffman says a big part of the decision is to "protect our business and meet regulations."
He clarifies, saying, "The first is that access to Reddit's data corpus has to be intentional. Today, the vast majority of unauthorized access to Reddit (basically the scraping and stealing of Reddit’s data) happens through our logged-out experiences. We will continue licensing our corpus intentionally, but those commercial deals come with guardrails that protect our users and our business. Any commercial deals give us the right to say what the data can and can't be used for and how it's presented. Without those guardrails and that intentionality, we can't control who has access to Reddit data, where things go or what they're used for."
It's not hard to see why Reddit would want to combat unauthorized scraping of its content. I know I've Googled questions I've needed answers to, only to get a bunch of answers in Google's AI overview that are essentially ripped straight from Reddit. It's in Reddit's best interest, then, to stop that from happening.
In a letter shared with shareholders, Huffman said that "our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter. The biggest impact was on logged-out and web traffic." Specifically, Huffman says, "During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week." And it doesn't take much of a stretch to connect that to AI overviews.
However, it does seem like there will be some limitations to Reddit's logged-in-only experience. According to the blog, the front page of Reddit will still be accessible without logging in, and you should be able to click on a direct Reddit link shared from a friend, and access that thread. But I get the impression that this system is still in the very early days, and the details of how exactly it'll work will emerge in the next few months.
Huffman says the next step will be "to test this in select markets outside the U.S. in the coming months." Based on those tests, Reddit will likely decide which content is going to be available for the general audience and which content is going to be walled off behind an account.
This isn't the first time in recent years that Reddit has drastically changed the way the website is run. Just last year, Reddit changed its mod removal policy after Huffman suggested the company would do so back in 2023. In the same year, Reddit also made access to its API for third-party apps more expensive.

item.title: IGN got the chance to bend Hideki Kamiya’s ear about the long-awaited Okami sequel at Lucca Comics and Games Festival 2026, where he shed some light on his creative process and addressed fans’ expectations about the upcoming title.
item.description:
IGN got the chance to bend Hideki Kamiya’s ear about the long-awaited Okami sequel at Lucca Comics and Games Festival 2026, where he shed some light on his creative process and addressed fans’ expectations about the upcoming title.
In December 2024 — almost 20 years after Okami was first released — fans of Clover Studio's critically acclaimed, cult-classic game were treated to news they never could’ve expected: a proper sequel was being made, led by the game’s original director, Hideki Kamiya.
Kamiya and Clovers, his new studio comprised of former Clover staff and industry veterans, are hard at work creating Amaterasu’s next adventure. And while he can’t say much about the project just yet, he did give us a smidge more insight about what the team has been cooking up over the last two years.
It’s safe to say Kamiya is keenly aware of players’ high expectations for the Okami sequel. It’s a tear-jerkingly beautiful game that’s been marinating in fans’ hearts and minds for two decades at this point, after all. But just as he approached the first game, he is once again planning to make an experience that appeals to both seasoned players and greenhorns alike.
“I created the first chapter of Okami keeping in mind that what I wanted to do was create a gaming experience that would be satisfying to relative beginners,” he told us via a translator, referencing Okami’s “sequence of commands for attacks.”
“When I created the plane sequences for Bayonetta — or even the game, itself — I had in mind players who were a little more experienced, obviously. Now that I’m making a second chapter of Okami, I’m going back to think about the more inexperienced or relatively new players. I still want to make it enjoyable for them, too,” he explained.
Kamiya is no stranger to kickstarting new franchises or creating sequels for pre-existing properties. (He did direct Resident Evil 2, after all.) But given the amount of hype from hardcore fans for the Okami sequel, he’s urging players to temper their expectations.
“[The Okami sequel] has become a sort of mission for me, because before, when I created a new game, I had no expectation from the public, of course. It was something completely new and, in a sense, unexpected. Now that I’ve created sequels, the expectation from the public has grown quite a lot, and I feel that. It’s better if you don’t have many expectations.”
When it comes to this new project, Kamiya doesn’t feel that his creative process has necessarily changed in the last 20 years. Instead, he says that he’s gained a sixth sense of a sort, where he can tell he’s going to make a mistake before it actually happens. (Which, I must admit, sounds like an especially useful skill to have.)
Screens - Okami HD
“As far as I can see, nothing has changed,” he mused when asked about how his process has evolved over the years. “The only thing I think is that, since I’ve made so many mistakes during my career, now, when I feel like I’m approaching a mistake, I can feel it beforehand. That’s the difference from then and now.”
Perhaps unsurprisingly, he couldn’t say much more about the Okami sequel. But what we did learn is that, just like its predecessor, this game will be accessible to newer players and seasoned gamers alike, appealing to both demographics just as the first one did.
For more Okami sequel news, you can check out IGN’s interview from early 2025 when we flew to Japan to chat with Kamiya, Kiyohiko Sakata, and Yoshiaki Hirabayashi, who told us that the next Okami game is a direct continuation from the first and not a side-story like Okamiden was.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: “The largest bank heist in human history.” That’s what Thursday’s $6.3 billion crypto hack of Binance is being called by insiders.
item.description:
“The largest bank heist in human history.” That’s what Thursday’s $6.3 billion crypto hack of Binance is being called by insiders.
Roughly $3 billion of the $6.3 billion in assets “had potentially been located and frozen across several exchanges, though it was not immediately clear if those funds were recoverable,” according to NBC News.
Binance said customer withdrawals should resume by Sunday, but deposits “remain unaffected and continue to operate as normal.”
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday that based on their investigation so far they suspect more than one hacker was involved in what he characterized as “a complex attack.”
“The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism … making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate,” said Teng.
Teng said that customer assets “are safe.” NBC said that Binance’s corporate holdings were the ones affected by the hack.
The North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor are reportedly suspected to be behind the attack on the cryptocurrency exchange, according to The New York Post.
“Cybercriminals swiped the digital coins out of Binance wallets within a mere 20 minutes starting at 4:30 p.m. ET Thursday, exploiting the system by hacking into an engineer’s laptop, according to analytics firm TRM Labs and industry insiders,” the Post reports.
The US Secret Service is helping in tracking the stolen crypto funds.
The hack rattled cryptocurrency markets and related stocks, with the likes of Bitcoin and Ether both enduring drops Friday.
Photo credit: Dan Kitwood/Getty Images.

item.title: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly cost $500 million to make, amid claims it has sold just over 400,000 copies.
item.description:
Gears of War: E-Day reportedly cost $500 million to make, amid claims it has sold just over 400,000 copies.
The Coalition’s action game launched on Xbox Series X and S and PC only, after Microsoft went down the console exclusive route following Asha Sharma’s arrival as Xbox CEO. As a Microsoft Studios game, E-Day also launched day one on subscription service, Xbox Game Pass.
This week, The Verge reported that E-Day had sold over 400,000 copies across console and PC. That’s a poor sales figure for any triple-A video game of Gears of War’s scope and prestige, but it could be an even worse commercial situation for Microsoft and The Coalition, given the extraordinary budget for E-Day.
The 100 Best Xbox Games of All Time
Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier rubber-stamped recent reports about E-Day’s budget in a video expanding on the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and the closure of BioWare.
“We just saw Gears of War: E-Day cost $500 million to Xbox. And that is a real number. That is real,” Schreier said. “That's what we're looking at here. That's what [AAA] games cost to make, especially in North America these days. And it’s driving these game companies to make layoffs, to do cost-cutting, to move development outside North America in a lot of cases, and to focus only on the biggest franchises that have as little risk as possible.”
The $500 million figure for E-Day was first reported by Kotaku, which said it was before marketing costs. IGN asked Microsoft for comment at the time, but it has yet to respond. It makes E-Day one of the most expensive video games ever made, and comes in at double the cost of some of its rivals. Bungie's recently released extraction shooter, Marathon, reportedly had a budget of over $250 million, for example. Concord's initial development deal was around $200 million, according to a report by Kotaku. In 2023, documents submitted as part of the Xbox Federal Trade Commission case accidentally revealed The Last of Us: Part II and Horizon Forbidden West each cost more than $200 million to develop. Last year, the astronomical development budgets of the Call of Duty games were revealed for the first time after a court document confirmed Activision pumped $700 million into Black Ops Cold War alone, although that was over the shooter's life cycle.
On October 13, a week after E-Day’s official release date, Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliott estimated that the game had generated $42.1 million in revenue, having sold 311,000 copies across Steam and Xbox. He also pointed to a boost to Game Pass subscriptions that appears to have been the result of E-Day’s release, although lamented the lack of a PS5 version, which may have generated increased revenue.
One question Microsoft may have when it comes to Gears is the impact on Game Pass. Has it made a big enough impact on the subscription service to offset disappointing sales revenue? With a budget in the $500 million range, can Gears of War: E-Day ever be considered profitable?
Discussing Xbox’s ongoing financial struggles this week, Sharma pointed to Minecraft and World of Warcraft Forever as setting records, and the critical acclaim Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 had enjoyed. No mention was made of Gears of War: E-Day.
Xbox Games Series Tier List
Xbox Games Series Tier List
What does this all mean for the future of the franchise? Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.
Eurogamer had reported on internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda.
The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently told the BBC that success for E-Day goes beyond sales, saying: "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware.”

item.title: Eiji Aonuma, the longtime producer of The Legend of Zelda franchise at Nintendo, is preparing to launch the highly anticipated remake of 1996's seminal The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time next week. And after so many years and so many Zelda games, you'd think it was routine for him. But it turns out he's nervous this time.
item.description:
Eiji Aonuma, the longtime producer of The Legend of Zelda franchise at Nintendo, is preparing to launch the highly anticipated remake of 1996's seminal The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time next week. And after so many years and so many Zelda games, you'd think it was routine for him. But it turns out he's nervous this time.
"I'm all nervous about releasing the remake of 'Ocarina' because I don't know how it's going to turn out, I can't stop thinking about it," he told AFP at a press event in Paris. The stakes are certainly a bit different this time around, as Aonuma and his team undertook the dauting task of remaking what many regard to be one of the greatest games of all time, as opposed to every other Zelda game they've made (well, almost) that is an original work.
As AFP notes, the original Ocarina of Time was the first project Aonuma worked on with legendary Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto. Now, he and his team are remaking it, and after we got to play it, we found it to be a bit more different than you might think if you're a veteran of the original. We also had someone who never played the original try it out if you're curious as to his impressions. Aonuma also talked about how some members of his team had never played the original – and he thinks that's a good thing.
If IGN metrics are anything to go by, Aonuma-san has nothing to be nervous about next week. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is IGN's second-highest-performing preview of the year so far (after, you guessed it, our preview of GTA 6). However, on our YouTube channel, it is #1 by a mile with over 1.8 million views.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake will be released on November 5. Stay tuned for IGN's review coverage, and in case you need to jog your memory or you're a first-time player, our game help guide is here for you.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has teased that Matt Reeves' long-awaited sequel has "an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology" that he doesn't "think has been seen before."
item.description:
The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has teased that Matt Reeves' long-awaited sequel has "an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology" that he doesn't "think has been seen before."
The face behind the mask of Gotham's Caped Crusader continued to lure in audiences with an interview shared by BAFTA yesterday. With filming back on track as The Batman Part 2 glides toward its early 2028 release date, Pattinson said its story will dive into Bruce Wayne's mind in a way that movies, shows, and maybe even comics have yet to explore.
"Still some ways to go, and the new script is… it's just amazing," he said. "It's just another completely different world.
The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel
"It's just an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology in a way that I don't think has been seen before. You know, when there's been hundreds and thousands of comics and so many different interpretations of the same character, it's like… it feels enormous, but really unusual, and unusual in a different way to the first one."
That's high praise from Pattinson, who helped deliver an already fresh take on Batman when he first starred as the DC comic book superhero in 2022. Reeves' vision of Gotham's grimy streets – and villain The Riddler (Paul Dano) – explored a quiet-but-edgy Bruce Wayne who eventually learned that vengeance won't change the past.
How The Batman Part 2 will examine a nearly 100-year-old character remains to be seen, but Pattinson is optimistic that the crew behind the flick has a few cards up its sleeve. Elsewhere in the interview, when recalling the days leading up to his involvement in The Batman, he said, "It's kind of universally acknowledged fact that Batman is the coolest superhero by a million miles." That's why he chose to make Batman his first foray into the superhero movie genre, and why he doesn't plan to hang up the cowl anytime soon.
Hot Toys Batman: Arkham Origins 1/6 Scale Figure Gallery
"When I first read the script," Pattinson said, remembering the process for the 2022 movie, "I was just thinking, 'Oh, there's something so immediately inspiring about it.' Batman's been reinvented so many times, and it's such an unusual reinvention, just in terms of the atmosphere of the movie.
"I really connected to it. It's just been one of those unbelievable experiences to shoot it, and I just want to keep doing it for as long as I can."
Following behind-the-scenes issues that saw Reeves take a small step back as Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh stepped in for assistance, The Batman Part 2 is still on track to premiere February 18, 2028. Pattinson called Soderbergh "completely selfless" for lending a hand.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Just in time for Halloween, HBO has revealed its casting for some key supporting characters in its Harry Potter TV adaptation.
item.description:
Just in time for Halloween, HBO has revealed its casting for some key supporting characters in its Harry Potter TV adaptation. The show has already revealed who will be its main cast, so now it's time to see which actors will add some undead color to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.
Shameless and Fargo actor William H. Macy is lending his voice to the Sorting Hat, and Nearly Headless Nick will be played by Leo Bill, who you might recognize from Apple's Foundation or in any number of period dramas. Laura Smyth from Netflix's Baby Reindeer will take on the role of the Fat Lady. Meanwhile, Andrew Brooke (Andor, The Agency) is the Bloody Baron, and Daniel Fearn (Slow Horses) is the Fat Friar, according to Deadline.
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone TV Show Character Images
We now have a pretty exhaustive cast list for the show, which will air on HBO on December 25. The big three, Harry, Ron, and Hermione, will be played by Dominic McLaughlin, Alastair Stout, and Arabella Stanton, respectively, and John Lithgow will portray Albus Dumbledore, and Paapa Essidu joins as Severus Snape.
On the official Harry Potter podcast last month, producer David Heyman spoke about translating the Harry Potter story into an episodic show instead of a series of feature-length films. "It's a slightly different beast, because you're telling a story over eight hours that you took two and a half hours to tell, and you have act breaks," he explained. "At the end of an episode, you leave on a question as opposed to an answer often. Or how do you lead into the next episode? So it's a different finding that structure. Finding that structure is just different. But boy, is it exciting."
Last month we got our best look yet at the series' upcoming first season with a trailer, while the second season is already filming.
